title: About a tenth of your skeleton is torn down and rebuilt every year
body: Bone is living tissue that is constantly being replaced. Cells called **osteoclasts** dissolve small patches of old bone, and **osteoblasts** follow behind to lay down fresh bone matrix, which then hardens with minerals. In an adult, about 10% of the skeleton's mass is remodelled like this each year. In a baby's [first year of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_remodeling), nearly the whole skeleton gets replaced.

cover.alt: The inside of a broken-open bone, showing a fine spongy mesh of thin bony struts beneath a dense outer wall

slides.heading: Who does what in your bones?
slides.explanation: Remodelling is a relay: osteoclasts clear a patch of old bone, then osteoblasts fill it in with new bone.

slides.heading: About 8 in 10 parts of your bone mass is dense cortical bone
slides.note: The spongy trabecular bone makes up the other 20%, but has about ten times the surface area

slides.heading: Bone follows the load
slides.text: Repeated stress, such as weight-bearing exercise, makes bone thicken at the points of greatest stress. Exactly how bone senses the load is still debated: one hypothesis is that bone gives off tiny electrical signals when it is squeezed.

slides.heading: Bones: fact or myth?

items.text: Adult bone is dead, unchanging tissue
A baby replaces nearly all its skeleton in year one
Exercise thickens bone where stress is greatest
Spongy bone has less surface than dense bone

slides.explanation: Bone is rebuilt all the time, and its spongy inner mesh has about ten times the surface area of the dense outer layer.
